app.inspector.help.bottom: The lower part of the frame read for dialogue. It must hold two-line subtitles too: 25–30 % is typical. Check it in Preview.
app.inspector.help.conf: Text read with less confidence than this is ignored (it still ends up in the review report). Lower it for difficult fonts, raise it to keep only sure text.
app.inspector.help.corr: Applies the replacements in corrections.txt (“wrong => right”, one per line): good for typos the OCR always makes, like names in difficult fonts. The list is in Settings › Lists.
app.inspector.help.fps: How many frames per second are read. 12 catches even very short lines and precise boundaries; 8–10 is a good compromise; 4–6 is fast but may miss short flashes. Time grows in proportion.
app.inspector.help.gap: In the review report, stretches without subtitles longer than this are listed as possibly missed lines.
app.inspector.help.ignore: Drops the phrases listed in ignore.txt (recurring watermarks, logos, fixed text). The list is in Settings › Lists.
app.inspector.help.lang: The language of the burned-in subtitles: it helps the OCR with accents and apostrophes. The menu lists the languages Vision reads on this Mac.
app.inspector.help.merge: Two lines with the same or similar text, closer than this, become one (typical in fades). Higher merges more, but may join lines meant to be separate.
app.inspector.help.mindur: Shorter lines are dropped as flashes (stray readings of 1–2 frames). They aren’t lost: the review report keeps them, ready to bring back.
app.inspector.help.multi: Each frame is read three times (Vision as is, Vision with more contrast, LiveText) and the reading with the most confidence-weighted votes wins. It fixes single-pass typos; it takes about three times as long.
app.inspector.help.refine: After the analysis, the start and end of every line are recomputed at the video’s own frame rate: about ±20 ms instead of ±40–120 ms. A few minutes more per episode.
app.inspector.help.report: Writes the review report next to the SRT: each line with a thumbnail and its confidence, doubtful lines highlighted, alternative readings, dropped lines and gaps. Almost free: keep it on.
app.inspector.help.sig_on: A second pass on the top of the frame for signs and translator notes. Their lines go in the SRT with {{\an8}}. Switch it off for series without signs: it halves the time.
app.inspector.help.skip: Skips the OCR of frames almost identical to the previous one. 0 reads every frame (best accuracy); 1 is about 20–30 % faster with the same timing; 2 or more is faster, with less reliable boundaries.
app.inspector.help.top: How much of the upper part of the frame is read for signs. 20–25 % is almost always enough.
app.inspector.help.topw: How much of the width, centred, is read in the signs band. Narrower keeps out watermarks in the top corners.
app.inspector.help.width: How much of the width, centred, is read for dialogue. 100 % if subtitles reach the edges; narrower keeps out corner logos but may cut long lines.
app.inspector.help.workers: OCR reads in parallel. It doesn’t change accuracy: the Neural Engine is the limit, so more than 4 helps little.
app.inspector.help.wrap: Longer lines are split into two or three balanced lines, preferably after punctuation and never inside a word. 36–44 is typical for players.
